newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed Burgan Bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed Burgan Bank stake.

text.p: Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) plans to sell 380 million out of its 440 million share majority stake in Burgan Bank through a two-stage privatisation, the official Kuwait News Agency said on Tuesday.
At the first stage 130 million shares will be sold in a public auction on July 31, a KIA official said. The minimum price for the share was set at 0.370 dinar ($1.22).
Burgan's share closed at 0.370 dinar on Tuesday.
The 22-year-old bank's total subscribed shares amounted to 743.4 million shares at the end of 1996. The state's holdings in the bank make some 59 percent of its issued shares.
Another 250 million shares will be put in a public offering whose date and share price would be set at a later stage, KIA, the state investment arm, said.
Kuwait has sold some $2.4 billion worth of shares in local firms since the launch of a privatisation programme in 1994. It plans to sell shares worth about three billion dollars.
Burgan Bank reported a net profit rise of 37 percent to 10.542 million dinars in 1996 calendar year.
Only nationals of the Gulf Arab states -- Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates -- can trade in Kuwaiti shares.
